headline: Genomic language model embeddings are benchmarked and adapted for viral and bacterial taxonomy and surveillance
label: Genomic Language Model Embeddings
summary: New preprints benchmark genomic language model embeddings against k-mer and MinHash baselines and adapt ProkBERT for pathogen surveillance.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluating and adapting pretrained genomic language models as embedding generators. One preprint compares DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM and Evo2-7B with k-mer and MinHash baselines for taxonomically informative embeddings of viral genome fragments. MicroDUET adapts ProkBERT with phylogeny and function adapter heads to produce compact embeddings for pathogen surveillance. What is new is the baseline-controlled assessment of embedding quality and the use of task-specific heads to impose structure on embeddings. The remaining items are adjacent rather than embedding-centered: RawMod applies a transformer to nanopore signal pileups, DeepHel uses multi-stage deep learning for Helitron annotation, and others address recombination inference, phylogenetic network dissimilarities and orthology benchmarking simulation. The items report methods and benchmarks, not deployed outcomes.
